summary:
🚀 NASA STEM Educational Game: Mars & Moon Colony Simulation
Project Summary for NASA Space Apps Challenge

1. Project Overview
An interactive 3D educational game for children ages 7–12 that teaches STEM concepts through planetary colonization. Players build and manage sustainable habitats on Mars and the Moon using official NASA data and mission parameters.

2. Core Features
🌟 A) Cyber-Blue UI & UX
Futuristic Interface: Deep space blue tones with glowing grids and a command-center design.

Top Navigation Bar: Fixed bar with sections (Home, Solution, Pricing, Sustainability, About, Contact).

Contacts Section: Highlights the lead developer, Moataz Ahmed.

🌐 B) Game Modes & Customization
Online/Offline: Choose single-player or cooperative team play with access codes.

Astronaut Customization: 3D preview to select NASA spacesuit colors and designs.

Environment Selection: Play on Mars (thin atmosphere, dust storms) or the Moon (Artemis base, extreme temperatures).

Mission Settings: Adjustable difficulty levels and survival durations.

🏗️ C) NASA-Accurate Equipment
Habitat Module: Pressurized protective domes.

Smart Greenhouse: Sustainable food and oxygen production.

Nuclear Reactor: Stable power source with a red warning glow.

Solar Canopy: Clean energy with automatic suit-recharging.

Rovers & Vehicles: Perseverance, Ingenuity helicopter, and Mars Ascent Vehicles.

🤖 D) Companion Robot & Learning
AI Guide: Presents engineering and science problems via multiple-choice
details:
Project Details & Submission Form

  • What does it do or how does it work? Our project is an advanced, interactive 3D educational simulation game designed for children aged 7–12, focusing on planetary colonization on Mars and the Moon. The game features a sequential user flow—starting with an immersive digital welcome screen, online/offline mode selection, team code integration or solo play, astronaut suit customization, and environment selection. Once inside the simulation, players manage colony infrastructure (such as Habitats, Greenhouses, Nuclear Reactors, and Solar Panels) while solving real-world STEM challenges presented by an interactive AI companion robot through multiple-choice quizzes.
    • Engine & Language: Developed using Godot 4 and GDScript for robust 3D mechanics and UI handling.
    • Frontend & Web Integration: Built with interactive web technologies, responsive UI design using custom styling, and modern layout structures to ensure seamless accessibility across devices.
    • Assets & Design: Utilized 3D models representing official NASA infrastructure (Artemis lunar bases, Mars rovers, nuclear reactors, and spacesuits).
